title: Alex's 'mm-hmm' and 'right' don't stop or restart its explanation

asked: Explain this first part to me in four or five sentences. Mhm. || Mm-hmm. || Right.
answer: Okay. We start with a mass thrown at speed v naught and angle theta, only gravity acting. So horizontally there's no force and the acceleration is zero. Vertically, the acceleration is minus g. We set the initial conditions: starts at the origin with velocity components v naught. Cosine theta and v naught sine theta. Integrating then gives constant horizontal velocity and a linearly decreasing vertical velocity. So, positions become x of t equals v naught cosine theta t, and y of t equals v naught sine theta t, minus one half g t squared. That sets us up to eliminate t and get the trajectory.

answer: Sure. We take the vertical position formula and set it to zero for landing, v naught sine theta t minus one half g t squared equals zero. Factor out t, giving t times v naught sine theta minus one half g t equals zero. One solution is t equals zero at launch, so we use the other piece, v naught sine theta minus one half g t equals zero. Solve that, and you get t equals two v naught sine theta over g. That is the full flight time. You can see it's twice the time to reach the peak. One moment, I'll walk it through. At the peak, vertical velocity is zero, so the max height comes out as v naught squared times sine squared theta, divided by two g.
